close_reason: Fixed: corrected OcspChecker struct doc and check_revocation_against_anchor doc to accurately describe behavior
description: pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs:63-64 and 210-216 — The limitation comment says: 'If the certificate has no OCSP URL (not supported in v0.1), the method returns Ok(()) (not-covered; same semantics as no OCSP source available).' But the method actually always parses the pre-loaded response and returns OcspStatusUnknown if no SingleResponse matches. It never checks the cert's AIA extension for an OCSP URL and never returns Ok(()) for 'no URL'. The correct v0.1 behavior is: the DER must be supplied at construction time; if it is, the response is checked; if no SingleResponse matches the serial, OcspStatusUnknown is returned. The Ok(()) claim in the doc is incorrect — the only Ok(()) case is CertStatus::Good. This should be corrected so callers do not expect soft-Ok on missing AIA.
title: OcspChecker check_revocation_against_anchor doc misleading: 'no OCSP URL' case
